text.p: The following are the main stories from Monday morning's German newspapers:

- CDU parliamentary leader Wolfgang Schaeuble says the solidarity tax will stay in place for long time. SPD reminds CDU of Chancellor Helmut Kohl's promise to remove the tax as part of 1999 tax reform. New debate over higher value-added tax.
- Greens reject coalition at federal level with reform communist PDS.
- New charges of wrongdoing raised against parliament president Rita Suessmuth in scandal she used military transport planes for private purposes.
- Fourth December Saturday calms the worries of retailers. Retail assocation HDE expects steady Christmas turnover. Cold weather helps sales of candy and winter sport clothing.

- New struggle over the president of the future European central bank breaks out. France's Finance Minister Jean Arthuis warns against placing too much emphasis on non-official French criticism of Germany.
- Interior Minister Manfred Kanther plans "revolution" in federal agencies by using private computer operators for state agencies.
- Retailers enjoy lively Christmas business. Shops filled on Saturday.
- Suessmuth wants to defend herself against "campaign" to discredit her.
- German government apparently planning to tax on-line services, according to report in PC magazine.
- Cartel office does not want to limit open access for natural gas companies. DIE WELT
- Suessmuth affair heats up, growing anger in the conservative CDU, CSU prepares for successor.
- Greens say "No" to coalition with PDS at federal level.
